definitionEn: a member of a group or organisation who knows private information about how it works
situation: Describing someone who works within a company, party or industry and knows what really happens behind closed doors.

examples.text: Written by a former minister, the book offers an [[insider]]'s view of how parliament really works.
According to one [[insider]], the company will announce hundreds of job cuts next week.
After twenty years in the business, she's a true [[insider]] who knows exactly who makes the decisions.

texts: Industry [[insiders]] expect prices to rise again in the spring.
Party [[insiders]] say the leader has already chosen her successor.
Tourists queue at the famous cafés, but [[insiders]] know where the locals eat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Insider — это человек, а не сведения. «Инсайд» в смысле утечки по-английски — inside information или a tip-off.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ trading is illegal in most countries.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Insider trading — торговля акциями на основе закрытой информации. Inner, interior и inward с trading не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Only an [[insider]] could have known that the director had secretly resigned.
nuance.explanationRu: Insider знает секреты, потому что сам находится внутри группы. Expert — специалист со знаниями, но тайные решения компании ему неизвестны.

reverse.text: We asked an [[expert]] to check whether the painting was genuine.
reverse.explanationRu: Подлинность картины проверяет expert — специалист. Insider — свой человек в организации, а не знаток.

fixIt.text: The journalist's story was based on information from an [[insight]] at the ministry.
fixIt.explanationRu: Insight — понимание, озарение. Человек, который знает, что происходит внутри министерства, — insider.

wordFormation.text: Tickets sold out in minutes because a few [[insiders]] had been told about the sale in advance.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How do you always hear about changes before they're announced?"
options: I read the company newsletter very carefully, like an insider of the news.
My friend in HR is a bit of an insider, so I sometimes get a hint.
Information is disseminated to me via insider channels, as per protocol.
reply.explanationRu: Insider — человек внутри организации, который знает её секреты. «Insider of the news» — бессмыслица, а третий ответ звучит как казённый отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

definitionEn: to officially visit a place or organisation to check that it meets required standards
senseNote: Базовое «внимательно осматривать» (B2) не берём: здесь inspect — официальная проверка заведений и оборудования.
situation: Officials from a government agency visit a school, restaurant or factory to check that it follows the rules.

examples.text: Health officials [[inspect]] every restaurant in the city at least once a year.
The factory was closed after officials [[inspected]] it and found serious safety problems.
Our school will be [[inspected]] next month, so all the teachers are polishing their lesson plans.

texts: Officials arrived without warning to [[inspect]] the kitchen.
The agency sends experts to [[inspect]] nuclear power stations every year.
Council staff must [[inspect]] the building before anyone can move in.

badCollocation.noteRu: Домашнее задание проверяют — check или mark. Inspect — официальная проверка заведений, зданий и оборудования.

collocationTask.prompt: The restaurant is ___ by health officials twice a year.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальную проверку описывает inspected. Controlled — «находится под управлением», revised — «исправлен», watched — просто «за ним наблюдали».

nuance.text: Two safety officials came to [[inspect]] the lift after it kept stopping between floors.
nuance.explanationRu: Inspect — проверить состояние по правилам. Control — управлять, держать под контролем: «проконтролировать лифт» по-английски не control the lift.

reverse.text: In the strong wind, the pilot struggled to [[control]] the small plane.
reverse.explanationRu: Управлять самолётом — control. Inspect значит «официально проверять», к управлению это не относится.

fixIt.text: The agency [[controls]] every care home once a year and publishes a report on each one.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Контролировать» в смысле официальной проверки — inspect. Control значит «управлять, держать под контролем».

wordFormation.text: Two [[inspectors]] arrived at the factory without any warning.

rewrite.original: Officials check the kitchen every six months.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the kitchen is inspected — «кухню проверяют».

definitionEn: an official check of a building, vehicle or organisation to make sure it meets standards
senseNote: Не просто «внимательный осмотр» (B1), а официальная проверка: школы, кафе, машины, безопасности.
situation: Talking about the official checks that restaurants, schools and vehicles must pass to prove they are safe.

examples.text: The restaurant was closed after it failed a hygiene [[inspection]] last month.
Every car older than three years must pass an annual safety [[inspection]].
Before the sale goes ahead, a surveyor will carry out a full [[inspection]] of the house.

texts: The school is preparing for a government [[inspection]] next week.
Customs officers carried out a random [[inspection]] of the lorry.
The bridge was closed for a safety [[inspection]] after the storm.

badCollocation.noteRu: Проверка знаний — test или assessment. Inspection — официальная проверка зданий, заведений и техники.

collocationTask.prompt: The building failed its fire safety ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальную проверку, которую можно пройти или провалить, называют inspection. Control — управление, revision — правка текста, overview — краткий обзор.

nuance.text: After a surprise [[inspection]], the care home was ordered to hire more nurses.
nuance.explanationRu: Внезапная проверка заведения — inspection (о финансах — audit). Revision — правка текста или повторение перед экзаменом, а не «ревизия».

reverse.text: The contract needs a small [[revision]] before we can sign it.
reverse.explanationRu: Правка в договоре — revision. Inspection — проверка зданий и заведений, текст так не исправляют.

fixIt.text: The café had to close for a week after a health [[control]] found mice in the kitchen.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Санитарный контроль» по-английски — health inspection. Control — управление, власть над чем-то, а не проверка.

wordFormation.text: The fire service will carry out an [[inspection]] of the theatre before it reopens.

reply.context: A friend who runs a café messages you: "The health inspectors are coming tomorrow and I'm panicking!"
options: Relax, your kitchen is spotless. You'll pass the inspection easily.
Lucky you! An inspection means they'll probably order lunch and leave a big tip.
Kindly ensure that all premises are rendered compliant prior to the inspection.
reply.explanationRu: Inspection — официальная проверка, её можно pass или fail. Второй ответ путает её с визитом гостей, третий звучит как распоряжение начальства, а не поддержка друга.

definitionEn: a natural feeling that tells you what to do or believe without conscious thought
senseNote: Не биологический инстинкт животных (B2), а человеческое чутьё: trust your instincts, my first instinct was to run.
situation: Explaining that you acted on a feeling rather than careful reasoning, for example when you sense that someone is lying.

examples.text: When the fire alarm went off, my first [[instinct]] was to grab my laptop.
Experienced nurses often trust their [[instincts]] when a patient seems fine but something feels wrong.
The figures looked convincing, but my [[instinct]] told me the deal was too good to be true.

texts: Trust your [[instincts]]: if the flat feels wrong, don't rent it.
The coach ignored his [[instincts]] and kept the tired player on the pitch.
Her political [[instincts]] told her the vote would be closer than expected.

badCollocation.text: have an [[instinct]] that he is lying
badCollocation.noteRu: С придаточным говорят I have a feeling that или my instinct tells me that. Сочетание have an instinct that звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.prompt: If the deal feels wrong, ___ your instincts and walk away.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчиво: trust (или follow) your instincts — «доверься чутью». Rely требует on, а hear и credit с instincts не сочетаются.

nuance.text: My [[instinct]] told me not to sign the contract until a lawyer had read it.
nuance.explanationRu: Instinct — внутреннее чутьё, которое подсказывает решение. Reflex — автоматическая реакция тела (моргнуть, отдёрнуть руку), она ничего не «подсказывает».

reverse.text: The doctor tapped my knee with a small hammer to test my [[reflexes]].
reverse.explanationRu: Врач проверяет reflexes — автоматические реакции тела. Instincts — чутьё и природные побуждения, молоточком их не проверишь.

fixIt.text: Something about the offer felt wrong, and my [[flair]] told me to walk away.
fixIt.explanationRu: Flair — талант или стиль (a flair for languages). Чутьё, которое «подсказывает», — instinct: my instinct told me.

wordFormation.text: When the lights went out, she [[instinctively]] reached for her phone.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Should I take the job? The salary is great, but the boss made me feel uneasy."
options: Take it! Your instinct of the salary is the most important thing.
Pursuant to my instinct, the offer ought to be declined forthwith.
I'd listen to that feeling. If your instinct says something's off, it probably is.
reply.explanationRu: Instinct — внутреннее чутьё, и третий ответ использует его естественно. «Instinct of the salary» — бессмыслица, а второй вариант звучит как юридический документ.

definitionEn: done or felt naturally and automatically, without thinking or being taught
situation: Describing a reaction or feeling that comes automatically, before you have any time to think about it.

examples.text: Covering your face when something flies towards you is a purely [[instinctive]] reaction.
Great comedians seem to have an [[instinctive]] sense of timing that can't be taught.
My [[instinctive]] response was to say yes, but I asked for a day to think it over.

texts: Most parents feel an [[instinctive]] urge to protect their children.
His [[instinctive]] dislike of the new manager proved to be justified.
Blinking is [[instinctive]]; nobody has to teach a baby to do it.

badCollocation.noteRu: Интерфейс, понятный без инструкций, — intuitive. Instinctive — о реакциях и чувствах, которые возникают сами собой.

collocationTask.prompt: I took an instinctive ___ to him the moment we met.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчиво: take a dislike to someone — «невзлюбить». С disgust, hostility и anger глагол take так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Shutting your eyes when sand blows into your face is [[instinctive]].
nuance.explanationRu: Instinctive — реакция, заложенная природой (зажмуриться, отдёрнуть руку). Impulsive — о человеке или решении: действует сгоряча, не думая о последствиях.

reverse.text: She's so [[impulsive]] that she once booked a holiday during her lunch break.
reverse.explanationRu: Человек, который поступает сгоряча, — impulsive. Instinctive описывает реакции, а не характер.

fixIt.text: When a ball flew towards her face, she raised her hands in an [[intuitive]] movement.
fixIt.explanationRu: Intuitive — о понимании без рассуждений или об удобном интерфейсе. Непроизвольное движение тела — instinctive.

wordFormation.text: Babies have an [[instinctive]] fear of loud, sudden noises.

reply.context: In a job interview, you're asked: "How do you make decisions under pressure?"
options: I make instinctive decisions only after weeks of careful analysis.
I rely on data, but in a real crisis my instinctive reaction is to stay calm and prioritise.
Honestly? I just go with my instinctive vibes, lol.
reply.explanationRu: Instinctive — «без раздумий», поэтому instinctive decisions после недель анализа — противоречие. Третий ответ слишком разговорный для собеседования.

definitionEn: relating to large organisations such as banks, universities or governments and the way they work
situation: Talking about banks, universities, courts or government bodies as organisations, rather than about the people who work in them.

examples.text: Pension funds and other [[institutional]] investors own most of the company's shares.
When experienced staff retire, a lot of [[institutional]] knowledge leaves with them.
The report calls for deep [[institutional]] reform, not just the dismissal of a few senior managers.

texts: Small charities often struggle to attract [[institutional]] funding.
Her thesis looks at [[institutional]] change in European universities.
Without [[institutional]] support, the volunteers' project quickly ran out of money.

badCollocation.noteRu: Студент вуза — a university или college student. Institutional описывает крупные организации и их устройство, а не учёбу в институте.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ investors such as pension funds and insurance companies
collocationTask.explanationRu: Пенсионные фонды и страховые компании — institutional investors. Official, organisational и structural с investors так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: After years in [[institutional]] care, he found it hard to cook and shop for himself.
nuance.explanationRu: Institutional care — жизнь в интернате, доме престарелых или детском доме. Organisational относится к организации работы (organisational skills), с care так не говорят.

reverse.text: The job requires excellent [[organisational]] skills and attention to detail.
reverse.explanationRu: Умение планировать и всё успевать — organisational skills. Institutional skills так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The charity gets most of its money from [[organisational]] donors such as banks and foundations.
fixIt.explanationRu: Банки и фонды как жертвователи или инвесторы — institutional donors, institutional investors. Organisational так не употребляют.

wordFormation.text: Museums increasingly depend on [[institutional]] sponsors rather than on ticket sales.

rewrite.original: Large organisations such as pension funds hold most of the shares.
rewrite.frame: Most of the shares are held by ____ such as pension funds.
rewrite.explanationRu: Банки и фонды в роли инвесторов — institutional investors.

definitionEn: to formally tell someone to do something, often as an official order
senseNote: Базовое «обучать» (instruct someone in something) не берём: здесь — официально велеть, дать указание.
situation: A manager, judge or official formally tells people what they must do, often in writing.

examples.text: The judge [[instructed]] the jury to ignore the witness's last remark.
Staff have been [[instructed]] not to discuss the merger with journalists.
Passengers are [[instructed]] to remain in their seats until the plane has come to a complete stop.

texts: The bank [[instructed]] its lawyers to recover the money.
Doctors [[instructed]] her to rest for at least two weeks.
Police [[instructed]] residents to keep their windows closed because of the smoke.

badCollocation.noteRu: Instruct — переходный глагол: instruct the staff to do something, без предлога to перед людьми.

collocationTask.prompt: Unless ___ otherwise, please keep this door locked.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Unless instructed otherwise — «если не будет других указаний». Teach и learn — про обучение, а explained otherwise в таком обороте не говорят.

nuance.text: The manager [[instructed]] everyone to delete the old files by Friday.
nuance.explanationRu: Instruct someone to do something — дать указание, велеть. Teach someone to do something — научить. Начальник здесь отдаёт распоряжение, а не учит удалять файлы.

reverse.text: My grandmother [[taught]] me to knit when I was six.
reverse.explanationRu: Научить вязать — teach. Instructed me to knit значило бы, что бабушка велела вязать.

fixIt.text: My manager [[entrusted]] me to prepare the budget report by Monday.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Поручить сделать» — instruct someone to do something. После entrust нужна другая конструкция: entrust someone with a task.

wordFormation.text: The staff followed the manager's [[instructions]] and left the building at once.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "Why is everyone working from home tomorrow?"
options: It has been instructed by the relevant authority that personnel remain domiciled.
Management instructed us to stay home while they fix the heating.
Management instructed us in staying home. It's part of a new training course.
reply.explanationRu: Instruct someone to do something — «велеть сделать», как во втором ответе. Первый звучит как казённый приказ, а в третьем instruct путают с «обучать».

rewrite.original: The manager told us to lock the office every evening.
rewrite.frame: We ____ to lock the office every evening.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив: we were instructed to do something — «нам велели».

definitionEn: playing an important part in making something happen or succeed
senseNote: Не музыкальное «инструментальный»: здесь be instrumental in doing something — сыграть ключевую роль.
situation: Giving someone credit for playing a key part in getting something done or making a change happen.

examples.text: Thanks to her fundraising, she was [[instrumental]] in setting up the town's first food bank.
Social media was [[instrumental]] in spreading warnings about the flood within minutes.
The new coach was [[instrumental]] in the team's return to the top division.

texts: Her advice was [[instrumental]] in my decision to change careers.
Volunteers were [[instrumental]] in rebuilding the village school.
This discovery was [[instrumental]] in developing the new vaccine.

badCollocation.noteRu: После instrumental нужен предлог in и форма на -ing: instrumental in winning the match, а не to win.

collocationTask.prompt: Her early research was ___ in bringing about the change.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be instrumental in doing something — «сыграть ключевую роль». Instructive — поучительный, insistent — настойчивый, incidental — второстепенный.

nuance.text: His contacts in the industry were [[instrumental]] in finding investors for the project.
nuance.explanationRu: Instrumental in — сыгравший ключевую роль в результате. Instructive — поучительный, дающий знания: an instructive visit, an instructive example.

reverse.text: The factory visit was very [[instructive]] for the engineering students.
reverse.explanationRu: Поездка, из которой студенты многое узнали, — instructive. Instrumental требует результата: instrumental in doing something.

fixIt.text: Her contacts were [[instructive]] in finding sponsors for the festival.
fixIt.explanationRu: Instructive — «поучительный». Сыграть ключевую роль в результате — be instrumental in doing something.

wordFormation.text: Local volunteers were [[instrumental]] in cleaning up the beach after the storm.

reply.context: At a leaving party, your boss asks you to say a few words about Anna, who is retiring.
options: Anna was very instrumental: she played the piano at every office party.
Anna's instrumentality in team formation is hereby formally acknowledged.
Anna was instrumental in building this team; most of us are here because she hired us.
reply.explanationRu: Be instrumental in — сыграть ключевую роль, как в третьем ответе. Instrumental не значит «играющий на инструменте», а второй вариант — канцелярит на тёплом прощании.

definitionEn: not enough in amount or quality for a particular purpose
senseNote: Формальное слово для официальных текстов; в разговоре обычно говорят not enough.
situation: Explaining formally that the money, time, evidence or information available is less than what is needed.

examples.text: The case was dropped because there was [[insufficient]] evidence to prove he was guilty.
The payment failed because there were [[insufficient]] funds in the account.
Staff complained that two weeks was [[insufficient]] time to learn the new software.

texts: The hospital's staffing levels are [[insufficient]] for the busy winter months.
A single heater is [[insufficient]] for a room this size.
Her written explanation was [[insufficient]], so the committee asked for more details.

badCollocation.noteRu: В разговоре говорят not enough money. Insufficient — официальное слово: insufficient funds в сообщении банка, insufficient evidence в суде.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Стандартная фраза банка — insufficient funds, «недостаточно средств». Lacking, absent и short перед funds так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Your card was declined due to [[insufficient]] funds.
nuance.explanationRu: Insufficient — «не хватает по количеству», а insufficient funds — стандартная банковская фраза. Inadequate чаще о качестве или о человеке: feel inadequate — чувствовать себя хуже других.

reverse.text: Surrounded by brilliant colleagues, he often felt completely [[inadequate]].
reverse.explanationRu: О чувстве собственной несостоятельности говорят feel inadequate. Insufficient описывает количество, а не человека.

fixIt.text: There was [[deficient]] time to finish the experiment, so the results are incomplete.
fixIt.explanationRu: Deficient — «с изъяном, неполноценный» (vitamin-deficient). «Недостаточно времени» — insufficient time.

wordFormation.text: Many new drivers are [[insufficiently]] prepared for driving at night.

reply.context: A client emails: "Why was my online payment rejected?"
options: The payment was rejected because the amount was insufficient: you paid too much.
Dude, your card's got insufficient cash, lol.
Sorry for the trouble. The bank reports there were insufficient funds on the card at the time.
reply.explanationRu: Insufficient funds — «недостаточно средств», вежливо и по делу. В первом ответе insufficient сочетается с «переплатой», а второй слишком фамильярен для клиента.

rewrite.original: There wasn't enough evidence to take the case to court.
rewrite.frame: The evidence was ____ to take the case to court.

definitionEn: a rude remark or action that shows a lack of respect for someone
senseNote: Не только грубое слово: предложение или поступок, унижающие человека, — тоже an insult (an insult to our intelligence).
situation: Reacting to a remark, offer or decision that makes you feel disrespected or treated as stupid.

examples.text: After twenty years of loyal service, a pay rise of one percent felt like an [[insult]].
The plot is so predictable that it's an [[insult]] to the audience's intelligence.
After the crash, the two angry drivers started shouting [[insults]] at each other.

texts: Don't take it as an [[insult]]; he criticises everyone's work.
Offering such a low price for her painting was an [[insult]].
To add [[insult]] to injury, the airline lost our luggage too.

badCollocation.noteRu: По-английски говорят cause offence или просто insult someone. Сочетания cause an insult нет.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение an insult to someone's intelligence — «нас держат за дураков». С mind, brain и wisdom так не говорят.

nuance.text: I only said his cooking was 'interesting', but he took it as an [[insult]].
nuance.explanationRu: Insult — само обидное слово или поступок: take something as an insult. Offence — обида: take offence (без артикля и as), а take something as an offence не говорят.

reverse.text: I hope you won't take [[offence]], but your report needs a lot more work.
reverse.explanationRu: Устойчиво: take offence — обидеться. Take insult по-английски не говорят.

fixIt.text: Calling her a beginner in front of the whole team was a deliberate [[abuse]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Abuse — неисчисляемое (verbal abuse), с артиклем a не употребляется. Одно обидное замечание — an insult.

wordFormation.text: Many readers found the article's tone deeply [[insulting]].

reply.context: A friend texts: "They offered me fifty pounds to design their whole website!"
options: That's not an offer, that's an insult. Say no.
Wow, what an insult! You should accept it immediately.
Such remuneration constitutes a grave insult to your professional standing, madam.
reply.explanationRu: Insult — унизительное предложение, и первый ответ это передаёт. Во втором insult противоречит совету согласиться, третий звучит как официальное письмо, а не ответ другу.

rewrite.original: His comment offended me, although he didn't mean it that way.
rewrite.frame: I took his comment as ____, although he didn't mean it that way.
rewrite.explanationRu: Take something as an insult — «воспринять как оскорбление».
